title: Additive ideal image equals tensor sections of the module quotient
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and J contained in I be quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Let r_K:A_X to (i_K)_*A_{Z_K} be the additive structure restriction [def-sc-etale-additive-structure-restriction]. Let F be the specified categorical module cokernel of J.toModules to I.toModules, and assume F is quasi-coherent. Then im(ker(r_I) to A_X to (i_J)_*A_{Z_J}) is isomorphic to ULift(F_et), where F_et is the tensor-sections sheaf [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. This assertion has no nilpotence or square-zero hypothesis.

source.place: Proof, Step 1 and its Claim; affine argument preserved in lem-sc-reduction-units-power-cokernel

proof.text: Define a as the specified ideal-module inclusion and f as restriction of additive vanishing functions to Z_J. Use the tensor ideal kernel presentation for J contained in I: choose e:T(I) to ker(r_I) and the limiting kernel fork T(J) to ker(r_I) to (i_J)_*A. Exactness follows from this limiting kernel fork.

In the abelian category of etale additive sheaves, the image of the second map is the cokernel of the first map. This is ShortComplex.Exact.isColimitImage. Compare the two categorical cokernels using coconePointUniqueUpToIso and transport along e using cokernel.mapIso.

The right-exact tensor-sections functor identifies the cokernel of T(a) with T(cokernel a), by PreservesCokernel.iso. Quasi-coherence of the specified cokernel identifies the latter sheafification with the given lifted tensor-sections sheaf, via sheafificationIso. Compose these isomorphisms.

proof_origin.place: T2 stage-3 reduction: kernel presentation, abelian image-cokernel theorem, and right exactness of sheafified tensor sections; preserves the affine argument of Steps 1-3.
